requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
**Verdict: not satisfied.** The implementation covers the obligations, but the `habeas status` output path has no test that carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.references.coverage.report`.

**Obligations**
1. `habeas status` MUST warn about every item without recent coverage.
2. `habeas author` MUST warn after it finishes.
3. Each warning MUST name file, line, kind and name.
4. Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.
5. A warning MUST NOT fail validation.
6. Repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.

**Implementation**
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` builds an `UncoveredItem` for each unreferenced item that no evidence read covers. `uncovered_error` formats the message as `file:line: kind name has no recent coverage…`, which names file, line, kind and name. `in_tests_module` sets `in_tests`.
- `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` drops `in_tests` items and filters the rest through `RecentCoverage`. That type reads the on-disk evidence plus the last N commits through `git2`, and reports when history is incomplete.
- `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warnings]` renders the "Coverage warnings" section of `habeas status`. It is called from `status_markdown_with_github`.
- `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warning_lines]` and `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` print the same warnings on stderr after `habeas author` finishes.
- Warnings are returned separately from the validation errors, and only the status and author paths call `warnings`. So validation neither fails on a warning nor reads Git history.

**Tests**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` carries `{test}` references to `requirements.references.coverage.report` and the three examples. It exercises three behaviours through `coverage_warning_lines`:
  - A never-read function (`helper`) is warned about at once.
  - A function inside `mod tests` (`fixture`) is not warned about.
  - Coverage lapses after three re-authorings, and validation does not fail on the warning.
- That test goes only through `coverage_warning_lines`, which is the author path. The `habeas status` path is separate code: `commands.rs#fn[coverage_warnings]` produces the Markdown section and the "Coverage history is incomplete" note.
- The only status-path test I found is `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]`, which asserts the `## Coverage warnings` section and a warning line. It carries `{test}` references to `requirements.cli.status`, `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and `requirements.references.definition_globs`, but not to `requirements.references.coverage.report`.

**Gap**
The status path and the author path produce this output through separate code. Only the author path has a test marked `{test}` for this subject; the status-path test exists but I found it only by searching. The `habeas author` printing in `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` also has no test.

There is no `{fixme}` acknowledging any of this.

`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every

{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,

:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
